correctness.rationale: The greedy occurrence times for each fixed pattern are independent geometric variables, yielding the displayed product transform. The shortest-border partition is unique and yields the weighted formal recurrence. At the unique root S(r)=1, squared letter weights sum below one; the correction is analytic, and a separate marker-event versus long-border union bound proves a strictly positive pole numerator. Positivity/aperiodicity give a unique dominant simple pole and the claimed residue. The binary square-root tilt is checked by substitution. The standalone rational-arithmetic verification reconstructs actual scattered subsequence sets for 30260 host words under six distributions, independently checks the weighted recurrence and confirms published uniform binary density; finite tests support, but do not replace, the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary full texts were compared at the level of claimed implication: Gabric establishes ordinary unbordered-language structure and ranking; Holub–Shallit establishes complete-word border probabilities; Biers-Ariel–Godbole–Kelley establishes unrestricted scattered-subsequence expectations; Cording et al. studies longest contiguous unbordered factors. Harju–Nowotka indexes fixed-weight unbordered pattern enumeration, but its full text was not available. None of the inspected full texts states the combined exact expectation for distinct unbordered scattered patterns under every iid bias or the tilted-source asymptotic fraction. published-finding corpus meaning queries and relevant previously catalogued research claims showed closest thematic findings without an implication. An unindexed combination of preexisting tools is the principal residual originality risk.

value.rationale: Unbordered (bifix-free) strings are a fundamental synchronization and pattern-matching class. Their frequency as distinct scattered patterns in a random independent host, rather than as complete words or contiguous factors, is a motivated natural complexity invariant. The theorem supplies an exact all-bias finite-length generating transform, proves a positive asymptotic fraction among unrestricted distinct subsequences, and identifies the non-obvious square-root tilt controlling the binary mean ratio. The weighted recurrence and uniform unbordered densities themselves are not presented as discoveries.
